PASS WITH NOTES -- performance review of #240
Head: 69c0516d8879793b1776753e6d75839931608ce0
Answers: 01a1eca5-e2a2-7c11-9342-3591a81a1be4

No performance blocker found. No local cargo build or test was run, no
dependencies were installed or linked, and no tracked product files changed.
This is the performance verdict; the separately assigned correctness and
security reviewers retain their scopes.

Cost by execution boundary

* Copilot status line: the existing managed refresh interval is 10 seconds
  per rendering Copilot session, PLUS event-triggered renders, not a hard
  one-render-per-10-seconds cap (claude_settings.rs:181-205). With C rendering
  sessions, the scheduled component is C/10 renders and whoami requests/s.
  The current roster has 119 rows, including 62 Copilot rows; that is not
  evidence that all 62 are live renderers.
* Per render: the same ONE whoami request as before, ZERO added daemon
  requests and ZERO added process launches. The pre-existing script execs
  pij-rs in its process; this does not mean the whole hook has zero process
  creation. The existing git fallback may still launch git for detached or
  ambiguous HEADs; this PR does not add or change that fallback.
* The added ownership check follows at most 64 parent reads and makes at
  most one start read, only if a candidate pid matches. The ordinary direct
  parent case is one parent read plus one start read. Wrapper shells add
  parent reads, not subprocesses or requests. macOS uses ProcBSDShortInfo
  for parents and ProcBSDInfo for the matching start; Linux reads /proc.
  observed_start is called directly, NOT ProcLiveness::proc_start, so this
  path cannot fall through to PsRunner. local/UTC packing is in-process.
  The functions fail closed if the kernel cannot answer. Sources:
  main.rs:2492-2515,2607-2616; statusline.rs:331-390;
  proc.rs:163-185,264-273,347-381.
* POST /v1/state: one additional native_receivers mutex acquisition and
  one-seat in-memory lease scan per card. No added store read, file read,
  launch or timer. The pre-existing native_receiver_reason read remains.
  GET /v1/cards also inherits this addition: one extra lease read per local
  card, O(N) total per bulk call, with the existing four-card concurrency
  bound. This shared call site should be included in the cost description.
* GET/POST /v1/seats: one additional mutex acquisition and O(N) lease scan
  per request, including requests made by extension registration paths,
  not just human list commands. Only local rows get the rendered suffix.
  IMPORTANT COST CORRECTION: projecting each local row then searches the
  lapsed vector with iter().find, so the complete addition is
  O(N + N_local * L), worst-case quadratic, not simply O(N). L is the
  number of eligible lapsed native Copilot rows returned by the scan.
  This is in-memory string comparison, after the lease lock is released;
  there is no per-row SQL, filesystem access or launch. At this fleet's
  size it is not evidence of a normal-use cost breach and does not block.
  Sources: http/mod.rs:3470-3501,3617-3648,4098-4129;
  delivery/mod.rs:536-578.
* No new poll, timer, renewal loop or daemon launch site. Lease renewal and
  expiry policy are unchanged. Lease age uses monotonic Instant::elapsed,
  not a wall clock; text construction adds only age formatting and strings.
  The ownership guard is display-only, a brake on naming a seat, not new
  seat-retirement or delivery policy.
